newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures regroup after Hashimoto scare.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures regroup after Hashimoto scare.

text.p: U.S. debt futures opened essentially flat Tuesday as the market reassessed the previous day's remarks by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

Hashimoto on Monday said Japan might be tempted to sell its U.S. Treasury holdings if the dollar fell sharply, sparking a downturn in financial markets. Treasury bond futures staged a mild selloff in the last 20 minutes of Monday's session, but stabilized overnight.
"The market for the most part has shrugged it off," said Jeff Feeney, research analyst for Smith Barney Inc.
Ministry of Finance officials later said that the comments had been misconstrued and that U.S. Treasuries are an essential investment tool in Japan.

The upcoming two-year note auction was keeping a lid on debt futures this morning, traders and analysts said. Treasury will sell $15.5 billion in two-year notes around midday, followed on Wednesday by $11.5 billion in five-years.
"The auctions will give us a sense of where Wall Street is on supply," said Rick Santelli, bond floor analyst for Rand Financial Services Inc.
Recent narrowing of spreads between government and corporate securities suggests that tight supply is forcing investors to accept more risk for less yield, Santelli said.
The general tight supply situation could bode well for the auction, analysts said. On the other hand, a relatively low yield of around six percent on the issue might dissuade buyers, they added.
U.S. consumer confidence data, to be released at 0900 CDT, is seen slipping to 126.3 from 127.1 previously.
For the session, traders were eyeing support at 111 24/32 and resistance at 112 13/32, a level September bond futures returned to repeatedly during Friday's session.
Tight ranges are expected to define the action in debt futures for the remainder of this week, but the following week holds the potential for greater volatility, traders and analysts said.

Compacted into a 3-1/2-day workweek that also marks the end of the second quarter will be purchasing managers' data, new home sales and personal income, plus a two-day Federal Open Market Committee meeting and the June employment report.
"Next week is going to be a bonanza," Feeney said.
September bond futures were 2/32 lower at 112-3/32, December Eurodollars were down 0.01 point at 93.93, and September 10-year note futures were down 1/32 at 108-16/32.
